How should SCRIPE route users after login, and should /hub remain the default entry?

Long image

A

Answer

SCRIPE must replace split client redirects with one backend landing waterfall across all 11 auth flows, auto-bypass /hub for single-workspace staff, and either rebuild /hub inside NexusLayout or retire it for NexusAppLauncher.

  1. Only 1 of 11 backend token-issuance handlers computes DefaultRedirectPath today, while passwordless, passkey, 2FA, refresh, and impersonation handlers return /.1
  2. Client hooks rewrite / to /overview and bounce unauthorized staff onto /hub, while TokenResponse.LastWorkspaceKey sits unused.2
  3. Six verified defects break /hub today: detached NexusLayout, unawaited menu fetch race, audit.view 403, static history rows, /settings 403, and blocked single-app bypass.3
  4. SAP Fiori, Odoo, Oracle Redwood, and Dynamics 365 all verify permissions live and auto-bypass the launchpad when a user holds one unlocked workspace.

1

Why does SCRIPE post-login routing drift today?

Diagram structure
  • AdminLogin PostLogin login_handler
  • 10 Token Handlers other_handlers
  • useLoginRedirect login_redir
  • RouteGuard Bounce guard_bounce
  • Detached /hub Shell hub_detached
  • AuditController 403 audit_gate
  • Unified Landing Resolver unified_resolver
  • NexusLayout Launchpad target_shell
  • login_handler → login_redir · / or /hub
  • other_handlers → login_redir · hardcoded /
  • login_redir → guard_bounce · /overview
  • guard_bounce → hub_detached · PBAC deny
  • hub_detached → audit_gate · audit.view
  • unified_resolver → target_shell · PBAC-verified

Only AdminLoginCommandHandler evaluates Admin workspace access, and even that check leaks when menu items have WorkspaceId == null or empty Resource. All other admin token flows default DefaultRedirectPath to /, forcing useLoginRedirect and RouteGuard to bounce non-admin staff across /overview before landing on /hub.4

  1. AdminLogin PostLogin ↗

    Only this handler computes DefaultRedirectPath; null WorkspaceId items can falsely count as Admin access.

  2. 10 Token Handlers ↗

    PasswordlessSessionIssuer, Passkey, 2FA, Refresh, and Impersonation omit DefaultRedirectPath and return /.

  3. useLoginRedirect ↗

    Maps / to /overview, routing module-only staff toward an Admin dashboard right after sign-in.

  4. RouteGuard Bounce ↗

    Rejects /overview access, calls findAlternativeWorkspaceRoute, and bounces non-admin users onto /hub.

  5. Detached /hub Shell ↗

    Renders outside NexusLayout, omits search and app-launcher handlers, and races unawaited menu fetches.

  6. AuditController 403 ↗

    Gates /api/v1/Audit/hub-summary behind audit.view, triggering 403 errors for module-only staff.

  7. Unified Landing Resolver ↗

    Target resolver evaluates permissions once on the server and routes into NexusLayout without client bounces.

How do SAP, Odoo, Oracle, and Microsoft handle post-login entry?

Enterprise platforms avoid raw static URLs per user because role changes and license downgrades quickly produce 403 errors. Instead, they bind roles or user preferences to workspaces and validate access at login.

PlatformEntry ModelSingle-Workspace RuleRole Default GovernanceUser Override

What does the 6-step post-login landing waterfall look like?

Diagram structure
  • Gate 0 Safety & Intent gate0
  • Tier 1 User Startup tier1
  • Tier 2 Role Priority tier2
  • Tier 3 Single Bypass tier3
  • Tier 4 Hub or Overview tier4
  • Tier 5 Zero-Access Safe tier5
  • gate0 → tier1 · pass
  • tier1 → tier2 · unset
  • tier2 → tier3 · unset
  • tier3 → tier4 · 2+ unlocked
  • tier4 → tier5 · 0 accessible

One backend IPostLoginLandingResolver service replaces all split auth redirects. It checks safety gates, user overrides, role priority, and single-app bypass against live PBAC and tenant entitlements.

  1. Gate 0 Safety & Intent ↗

    Enforces MustChangePassword, PendingPayment, or a safe ?redirect parameter verified against current permissions.

  2. Tier 1 User Startup ↗

    Reads AdminPreference startup choice (auto, hub, or workspaceKey) if tenant admin policy permits user overrides.

  3. Tier 2 Role Priority ↗

    Evaluates assigned Role records ordered by Role.Priority ascending to pick the first permitted DefaultWorkspaceKey.

  4. Tier 3 Single Bypass ↗

    Counts only unlocked workspaces; when count equals 1, jumps straight to that workspace's HomeRoute.

  5. Tier 4 Hub or Overview ↗

    Sends Admin-capable multi-workspace users to /overview and module-only multi-workspace users to /hub.

  6. Tier 5 Zero-Access Safe ↗

    Sends accounts with zero accessible workspaces to /account/dossier instead of triggering redirect loops.

What 6 defects break /hub right now?

Six code-level defects make /hub fail even when a user reaches it intentionally. Fixing /hub requires mounting it inside NexusLayout and replacing audit.view dependencies with a self-scoped launchpad contract.

Which target option fits SCRIPE best?

Every login must run through a single server resolver regardless of UI choice. The open product decision is whether multi-workspace non-admin managers still need a dedicated /hub page when NexusAppLauncher (⊞) already exists.

OptionSingle-Role UXMulti-Workspace Non-Admin UXMaintenance & ScopePrimary Trade-off
Approach A: Waterfall + Rebuilt /hubDirect to primary workspace (0 extra clicks)Best BalanceRole-safe /hub launchpad inside NexusLayoutMedium: backend resolver + role-config UI + /hub remakeTwo launchpad surfaces (/hub and ⊞ modal)
Approach B: Direct Entry (Retire /hub)Direct to primary workspace (0 extra clicks)Opens highest-priority workspace; switch via ⊞Lowest DebtLowest: retire (hub) route and HubSidePanelCross-module managers lose a neutral landing summary
Approach C: Universal /hub (Odoo Style)Daily Click TaxForced onto /hub on every loginRebuilt /hub launchpad inside NexusLayoutHigh /hub dependency for all usersSlows down front-desk and coach workflows daily
